title: Stochastic Quant Cost Curve Explorer
content:
Purpose:
This sheet is an exploratory playground for building stochastic cost/latency/quality curves across quantization options (FP16 baseline, FP8 variants, INT8 dynamic/static, and 4-bit post-training / GPTQ). The goal is a compact calculator teams can use to estimate per-token unit economics and recommended quant choices for different SLOs and workload shapes.

Context / why this exists:
- We have many one-off spreadsheets for quantization impact; this is trying to centralize a heuristics-driven scenario explorer that trades TTL (tail latency), throughput (tokens/sec), unit cost ("+$ per M tokens"), and expected quality delta (negative log-likelihood or eval delta).
- Not a canonical pricing model; meant for internal product/solutions use in sizing Dedicated and Private proposals and for recommending quant profiles in Redwood Optimize.

High-level assumptions (editable fields):
- Baseline model: name + FP16 baseline perf (tokens/sec, p95 latency at batch=1)
- HW profile: gpu type (A100-40, H100, T4), price/hr (on-prem equivalent), inference concurrency factors
- Batch size distribution: p50/p90 batch sizes; average effective batch = weighted avg
- Requests per minute (rpm) and token distribution: average seq length, prefix reuse rate (cache hit %), kv-cache savings exponent
- Costing: GPU hr cost -> cost per second -> cost per token = (1 / tokens_per_second) * cost_per_second, adjusted for batching and concurrency
- Quality model: expected BLEU/ROUGE/EM/LM delta per quant choice (user-provided or default heuristics derived from offline evals)

Input columns (sheet layout suggestion):
- scenario_id (free text)
- model_family (e.g., Llama-2-13B, Red-Base-7B)
- baseline_fp (FP16|BF16) tokens_per_sec_baseline (numeric)
- hw_type (A100/H100/T4)
- gpu_cost_per_hour_usd
- avg_request_tokens
- avg_response_tokens
- avg_batch_size
- cache_hit_pct
- quant_profile (none|int8-dyn|int8-static|fp8-e5m2|4bit-gptq)
- throughput_multiplier_vs_baseline (auto-calc or override)
- p95_latency_multiplier_vs_baseline (auto-calc or override)
- quality_delta_pct (negative = worse, positive = better)

Auto-calculated columns (formulas described):
- tokens_per_second_effective = tokens_per_sec_baseline * throughput_multiplier_vs_baseline * (1 + cache_hit_pct * cache_speedup_factor)
- cost_per_token_usd = (gpu_cost_per_hour_usd / 3600) / tokens_per_second_effective / effective_concurrency
- cost_per_request_usd = cost_per_token_usd * (avg_request_tokens + avg_response_tokens)
- annualized_cost_estimate = cost_per_token_usd * total_tokens_per_year (user input)
- latency_p95_ms = baseline_p95_ms * p95_latency_multiplier_vs_baseline * (1 - batching_latency_reduction_function(avg_batch_size))

Heuristic defaults (editable):
- throughput multipliers: INT8-dyn = 1.6x, INT8-static = 1.4x, FP8-e5m2 = 1.35x, 4bit-gptq = 2.4x (best-case)
- p95 latency multipliers: INT8-dyn = 0.95x, INT8-static = 0.9x, FP8-e5m2 = 0.95x, 4bit-gptq = 0.75x (note: quant noise may increase variance -> watch tails)
- quality delta guidance (avg across open models): INT8-dyn = -0.3% eval, INT8-static = -0.8%, FP8 = -0.4%, 4bit-gptq = -1.6% (high variance by model/task)
- cache_speedup_factor: 0.25 (i.e., cache hits reduce work by 25% on average)
- effective_concurrency default: 1.0 (teams should change for multi-tenant or higher qps)

Scenario examples (rows to try):
- Low-latency chat (batch=1, avg tokens 32 in/out, p95 target < 150ms) -> favors FP8 or FP16 if quality critical; 4-bit often fails tail SLO without increased concurrency or dedicated HW tuning.
- High-throughput embedding-generation (batch=64, avg tokens 1) -> 4-bit or INT8-static may be best; cost per embedding drops sharply with batch.
- Regulated enterprise LLM (on-prem H100, must maintain <0.5% quality delta) -> prefer INT8-dyn with conservative heuristics; include a quality safety margin column.

Quality vs Cost frontier pane (how to visualize in the sheet):
- X axis = cost per 1M tokens (USD), Y axis = expected quality delta (relative to baseline) -> plot points per quant_profile per HW type. Color by p95_latency_MS bucket. Add hover text for batch size and cache hit.
- Also a stacked bar view of cost components: GPU time, host overhead, memory swap penalties (rare), and amortized pre/post processing.

Recommended decision rules (rule-of-thumb outputs):
- If p95_target_ms <= baseline_p95_ms * 0.85 -> avoid 4-bit unless proven with latency tail testing.
- If quality_delta_pct < -1.0% and task is generation-sensitive (summaries, code) -> prefer INT8-static or FP8 with eval set check.
- If avg_batch_size >= 16 and seq_len <= 8 -> 4-bit is recommended candidate (run offline eval + calibration).
- If on-prem with low GPU cost/hr and high qps -> prioritize throughput gains; cost per token less decisive.

Open questions / TODOs (short):
- Get updated real-world throughput multipliers for Red-Base and Red-Large series on H100 (OPT-1287).
- Add per-layer GPTQ sensitivity map (not just global 4-bit) -> need bench harness output format.
- Bake in Redwood Optimize suggestions: map workload to a recommended quant_profile + confidence score.
- Add variance propagation: show p95 tail increase probability with 4-bit for small batch sizes.

Quick example CSV snippet for copy/paste into a visualization sheet:
scenario_id,model_family,baseline_tps,hw_type,gpu_usd_hr,avg_batch,cache_hit,quant_profile,throughput_mult,p95_mult,quality_delta
chat-lowlat,Red-Base-7B,120,A100-40,6.5,1,0.1,fp8-e5m2,1.35,0.95,-0.4
embed-bulk,Red-Base-7B,800,H100-80,12.0,64,0.02,4bit-gptq,2.4,0.75,-1.6
enterprise-secure,Red-Large-13B,60,H100-80,12.0,2,0.2,int8-dyn,1.6,0.95,-0.3

Notes on validation:
- Cross-check against microbench results (GH: redwood-inference/benchmarks#342) and the confluence quant-benchmarks page. Use at least 3 seed runs for noisy 4-bit numbers.
- Where possible, use real downstream task evals (QA, summarization, code) rather than LLM perplexity alone.

Suggested next steps for product/solutions engineers: 
- Convert this sheet into a small Redwood Optimize widget prototype (inputs -> compute -> frontier plot) and validate with 5 pilot customers.
- Run the 4-bit GPTQ sensitivity harness on Red-Base & Red-Large on H100 (ticket OPT-1287) and pull realistic throughput multipliers into the heuristics tab.
- Draft short runbook for "safe quant rollout" that pairs recommended quant profile with a canary eval prompt set and automatic fallback policy.

Appendix: shorthand formulas to paste into sheet cells (example Excel/Sheets friendly)
- tokens_per_second_effective = =C2*D2*(1+E2*0.25)  
  (C2=tokens/sec baseline, D2=throughput multiplier, E2=cache_hit_pct)
- cost_per_token_usd = =(gpu_usd_hr/3600)/tokens_per_second_effective/F2  
  (F2=effective_concurrency)
- latency_p95_ms = =baseline_p95_ms * p95_mult * (1-0.12*LN(1+avg_batch))  

Contact / owner notes: Aisha Kapoor (product-optimize) — use this as a working sheet, keep heuristics conservative until we have H100 datapoints. Leave comments inline, flag any numbers copied from other teams.
